solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ring in excellent condition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ring is literally to ... does
second meaning: the idiom for something in perfect working order or perfect health

explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase literally and it describes what a bell does when struck; read it as an idiom and it means perfectly sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person or machine in perfect health or working order, while its literal reading is simply what ringing is.

clue.text: Crime of one type of criminal

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.surface: A question about which offence a certain kind of crook typically commits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is taken as it stands, not as a link word; a fence is someone who deals in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law, the general sense of a crime.

clue.text: 12 divided by 50, carrying one over, finishes as previously

indicators.note: the word for 12 is split in two by the numeral placed between its halves

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock, so the number stands for the word noon
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: the finishes are the final letters of the three words carrying, one and over

explanation.surface: A schoolroom long-division sum, complete with carrying a digit, reaching its end just as before.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a cross-reference to 12 across, but it is the time of day. 'divided by' puts L into NOON as NO L ON; 'finishes' takes the last letters of carrying, one, over to give GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened as previously but no more is something that has stopped: the phrase marks a former state that has ended.

clue.text: Primates turning tail in this part of the church

indicators.note: only the tail end of the word for primates, its last two letters, is turned round

parts.note: apes are primates

explanation.surface: Monkeys fleeing from a section of a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' looks like running away, but it reverses just the last two letters of APES.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Having a dab hand will produce no disaster

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are worked into something new, a rearranged form

explanation.surface: Reassurance that a skilled practitioner won't make a mess of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is an expert, so having one's skill amounts to deftness and dexterity.

clue.text: Throw out former politically extreme leftist leaders

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: the leaders of the three following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A call to eject a party's onetime hard-left figureheads.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force someone out of a party, school or place, the same as throwing them out.

clue.text: Monarchy love to be in fancy hotels

indicators.note: the letter for love goes inside the rearranged letters of hotels
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, so the letters of hotels are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone longing to stay in luxurious hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reads as a verb of desire but rearranges HOTELS into LESTHO, with O put inside as LES-O-THO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a kingdom in southern Africa, ruled by a king, so it is a monarchy.

clue.text: Comedy of deception

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally humorous material, funny stuff
second meaning: the idiom for underhand trickery or shady dealing

explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally the phrase is the business of being funny; as an idiom it means trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names suspicious or dishonest goings-on, while the literal words describe the trade of comedians.

clue.text: Business folk have seen Turner perform

indicators.note: the tail of the word perform, used as a verb: to form is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new order

parts.note: the first three letters of perform, taken as they stand

explanation.surface: Executives who have watched an artist or singer named Turner on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perform' looks like one word but splits in two: its first three letters join the fodder, and 'form', a verb meaning shape, is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrepreneurs are people who set up and run businesses, taking financial risks for profit.

clue.text: Found special case confusing as the story develops

indicators.note: confusing means mixing up, so the letters are jumbled
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A detective finding an unusual case baffling while the plot develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the outside letters of special, S and L, to join FOUND before the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: When a story unfolds, it reveals itself gradually, which is what a developing plot does.

clue.text: Persuades awkward person to house one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the numeral inside them, as a house holds a resident
awkward means clumsy or out of shape, so the letters of person are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone talks a difficult individual into accommodating a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' turns PERSON into ROPESN, and I goes inside as ROPES-I-N.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope someone in is to talk them into taking part, an informal way of saying you persuade them.

clue.text: Fabric or linen, in one piece

indicators.note: a piece of the words is taken, a run of letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A choice between some material and linen made as a single length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one piece' sounds like a seamless garment, but the letters run across linen, in and one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric of silk or nylon, used for dresses and curtains.

clue.text: Miscreant's instrument backing rubbish

parts.note: the viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for rubbish is turned round

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: An offender's musical instrument provides support for nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' sounds like musical accompaniment, but it reverses ROT to TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A violator is someone who breaks a law or rule, an offender or wrongdoer.

clue.text: Each Celtic half-back getting furious

parts.note: a pop means each, as in a pound a pop

indicators.note: half of the word Celtic, its front half, is turned back to front while the rest stays put

explanation.surface: A defender in Celtic's football team losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-back is a football position, and Celtic is a Glasgow football club; here the phrase turns back the first half of the name, CEL becoming LEC before TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplectic means so angry as to seem close to a fit, an emphatic way of being livid.

clue.text: Making a noise about stretch of apiculture

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for making a noise surrounds the word for stretch

parts.note: beeping is making a short electronic noise
to eke is to stretch out a supply

explanation.surface: Buzzing about during a spell of bee-keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' is the verb eke, as in eking out supplies, not a period of time; 'about' wraps the bleeping word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiculture is the formal term for keeping bees, from the Latin apis, bee.

clue.text: Backwater circuit

indicators.note: the front of the word Backwater tells the solver to read the word for water backwards

parts.note: a pool is a body of water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Backwater' looks like one word, a quiet stretch of river, but splits into Back, a reversal signal, and water.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a closed path that returns to its start, as a circuit does.

clue.text: In the morning to be found in island with a West country offering

indicators.note: the morning abbreviation sits inside the island's name

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A morning visit to an island, with a regional dish being served.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; a cream tea is scones with clotted cream and jam, a Devon and Cornwall speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream teas are the classic treat served to visitors in Devon and Cornwall, so they are that region's offering.

clue.text: Month nine, or seven, in Paris for part of Irish family

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the abbreviation for September, the ninth month
second meaning: the French word for seven
third meaning: a branch of an Irish or Scottish clan

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one short word: an abbreviation, a French number and a clan division.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a subdivision of a clan, especially in Ireland, descended from a common ancestor.

clue.text: New King's heart dropped after constant drink

indicators.note: after places the constant first, with the remaining letters following it

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant

indicators.note: the heart of the word for king, its middle two letters, is dropped down to the bottom of the word

parts.note: the word king, its 's being the link to heart

explanation.surface: A newly crowned king turns faint and keels over after a steady stream of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart dropped' does not delete the middle letters: it moves IN from the centre of KING to the end, giving KGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink gin is gin flavoured with Angostura bitters, a traditional naval cocktail.

clue.text: Perhaps too badly misplaced by grocers

indicators.note: badly here means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that grocers' signs misuse punctuation, as in 'banana's'.
explanation.walkthrough: The grocer's apostrophe is the stray mark in signs such as 'potato's for sale'.
explanation.definitionFit: The grocer's apostrophe is the well-known punctuation error of using a possessive mark in a plural on shop signs.

clue.text: Wild leopard set free

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild big cat released back into its habitat.
explanation.definitionFit: A paroled prisoner is released early on condition of good behaviour, so is let out of jail.

clue.text: Where to find pink gin and score? Not quite

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the drink is the answer to clue 19 in this grid
second meaning: a score is twenty, and just short of that is one less

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cross-reference: the drink in question is the answer at 19 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The number sits one below a score of twenty, and is also the clue number where the drink appears.

clue.text: Times gripping little message

indicators.note: the two letters hold the word for little between them

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them stand for times
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A newspaper holding a brief note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is two time abbreviations, T and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short message posted on the social network formerly called Twitter.

clue.text: A European, mostly OK

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last, so the word for European loses its final letter

parts.note: a Greek is a European

explanation.surface: Approval from a continental, given with some reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: To say OK to something is to consent, to go along with it.

clue.text: Try and use a knife

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is an attempt, as in have a ... at it
second meaning: to pierce with a blade

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both an informal attempt and the act of driving in a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something means making an attempt, while the verb means wounding with a pointed weapon.

clue.text: Firm providing cover for FBI division

indicators.note: the word for firm wraps round the agents, covering them

parts.note: set means firm, fixed
G-men are FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: A company acting as a front for a branch of the American police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing cover' sounds like a spy's front business; G-men is old slang for FBI agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one of the parts something is divided into, a section or portion.

clue.text: City centre turns ultra-fashionable, but in name only

indicators.note: turns means turns round, so those middle letters are read backwards
the centre of the word city is its middle two letters
to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters of ultra are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A city's downtown suddenly becomes extremely trendy, though only nominally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultra-fashionable' looks like one hyphenated word, but splits into the fodder ultra and its anagram signal; 'City centre' is the middle two letters of City.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular head holds a title without real power, so the role exists nominally.

clue.text: Steam or water gets on deck: read announcements here

parts.note: steam or water is H2O in a form that is not ice
to board a ship is to get on its deck

explanation.surface: Steam or spray coming aboard a ship, where passengers read the notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steam or water' is a riddle: both are forms of H2O that are not ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices are pinned up on these boards in offices and schools so people can read news and announcements.
